title: Revenue Integrity Specialist
description:
Raventra Health is a medical services company providing outsourced billing, coding, and claims processing solutions for provider groups and hospitals. As a Revenue Integrity Specialist, you will help provider clients identify and prevent revenue leakage across the revenue cycle. You will review charge capture, billing workflows, payer reimbursement, and account activity to identify discrepancies and opportunities for improved accuracy, compliance, and reimbursement.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Review charge capture and billing workflows to identify missed or inaccurate charges

  • Analyze claims, payments, adjustments, and reimbursement data to identify revenue discrepancies

  • Identify potential revenue leakage and recommend corrective actions

  • Review payer reimbursement against contracted rates and established billing guidelines

  • Investigate underpayments, incorrect adjustments, and other payment discrepancies

  • Collaborate with billing, coding, payment posting, and AR teams to resolve revenue-related issues

  • Monitor recurring billing and reimbursement trends and identify opportunities for process improvement

  • Prepare reports and communicate findings and recommendations to internal teams and client stakeholders

  • Support audits and reviews related to charge capture, billing accuracy, and reimbursement

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

  • 2+ years of experience in revenue integrity, healthcare revenue cycle management, medical billing, or a related healthcare finance role

  • Strong understanding of healthcare billing, claims, payments, and reimbursement processes

  • Experience analyzing charges, payments, adjustments, and payer reimbursement

  • Ability to identify discrepancies and investigate the root cause of revenue leakage

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with excellent attention to detail

  • Ability to interpret billing and reimbursement data and communicate findings clearly

  • Strong understanding of payer requirements and healthcare revenue cycle workflows

  • Ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities in a remote environment

  • HIPAA-compliant private workspace

NICE TO HAVE

  • Experience reviewing payer contracts or reimbursement rates

  • Medical coding or billing knowledge

  • Experience with Epic, Athena, eClinicalWorks, or another major EMR or practice management system

  • Experience with revenue cycle reporting and data analysis

  • Experience working with provider groups or hospitals

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

Compensation will be discussed during the interview and will reflect the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and relevant healthcare revenue cycle expertise.

Benefits and additional employment details will be discussed during the hiring process.

HIRING PROCESS

Application review → introductory conversation → hiring manager interview → offer.

We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. Built on Enverus ONE™, it combines voice-first access, real-time operational inputs like weather and equipment context, and company-specific safety procedures to support workers in dynamic field environments where conditions, crew configurations, and risks shift constantly.   • Database programming experience with Postgres (or similar) and Python
  • Good understanding of algorithms and data structures
  • Experience with modern application/data development tools
  • Experience with Agile methodologies
  • Experience with modern CI/CD

Python, Postgres, Snowflake, Databricks, microservices, AWS, Go, Kubernetes, GitHub, Confluence, and Jira.

title: Senior Program Manager, Leadership Programs
description:
About CDI

The Constructive Dialogue Institute (CDI) is a non-partisan, non-profit dedicated to equipping the next generation of Americans with the skills to communicate and collaborate across lines of difference. We work with U.S. colleges and universities by providing co-curricular programming for students, professional development for faculty and staff, and strategic guidance to leadership. Our goal is to foster constructive dialogue at every level of the institution and to create the conditions for lasting organizational change. CDI was co-founded by psychologist Jonathan Haidt, the bestselling author of The Righteous Mind and The Anxious Generation.

About the Role

CDI seeks an experienced, highly organized Senior Program Manager to serve as the operational backbone of the Leadership Institute (LI), CDI's program to equip senior higher education leaders with the strategy, tools, and peer network to advance cultures of inquiry and dialogue on their campuses. This full-time, remote role works closely with the Vice President of Leadership Programs to run LI's full-year arc: the fall Summit, monthly institutional coaching, quarterly Peer Learning Communities, and each cohort's measurement and reporting cycle.

In your first 90 days, you'll learn LI end-to-end by shadowing coaching calls and supporting Summit planning, getting fluent in our systems and templates, and planning for the year-long engagement. By month three, you'll independently manage scheduling and logistics for our Leadership Institute partners.

By month six, you'll manage the operating rhythm for the full cohort year, tracking institution progress, flagging risks to the VP, running day-to-day partner communication, and recommending process improvements.

Within your first year, you'll be a trusted first point of contact for campus teams on coordination and progress, and a trusted operational partner with the VP.

The ideal candidate thrives at the intersection of program operations and relationship management: strong execution, an instinct for spotting opportunities and process improvements, and good judgment about what to flag versus solve directly. The Senior Program Manager reports to the Vice President of Leadership Programs.

Responsibilities

Program & Portfolio Management

  • Own the schedule and tracking systems for the full LI cohort's year-long arc, including summit prep with the institution teams, monthly coaching, and quarterly Peer Learning Community sessions

  • Keep the Vice President and broader team ahead of deadlines across all concurrent workstreams, within and across cohort years.

  • Track each institution's strategic priorities throughout the year and escalate stalled progress or risks.

  • Identify and design improvements to LI's operating systems and templates (discovery process, communications cadence, reporting formats) in partnership with the VP.

Institution & Partner Liaison

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for institutional teams on scheduling, onboarding, pre-work, and follow-up across the full year.

  • Field routine questions and troubleshoot logistics directly.

  • Spot opportunities raised by campus partners and elevate them to the VP

Cross-Team Coordination & Communication

  • Manage meeting cadence and information flow among the VP, consulting, partnerships, and impact teams

  • Maintain and organize program materials, including discovery reports, session decks, PLC, and coaching resources

  • Model clear, professional communication in every touchpoint with institutional partners

Data Tracking & Reporting

  • Track Pillar-specific progress and coaching-call reflections across the cohort.

  • Synthesize cohort-wide data into formats leaders can act on, including progress dashboards, insights reports, and summaries.

Requirements

About You

  • An experienced program manager. You bring 5+ years of program or project management experience, ideally spanning cross-functional or partner-facing work in education, consulting, or nonprofit settings.

  • A skilled portfolio juggler. You're comfortable managing a complex, multi-institution portfolio and tracking multiple workstreams at once.

  • A proactive process-improver. You have a track record of independently identifying and proposing improvements, not just executing what's handed to you.

  • A trusted external liaison. You're comfortable liaising directly with external partners on defined pieces of work, with good judgment about what to resolve independently versus escalate.

  • Data-savvy. You can pull information from multiple sources (surveys, interviews, documents) into a clear, decision-ready narrative.

  • A strong communicator. Your written and verbal communication is excellent, calibrated for both internal teams and senior higher-ed leadership.

  • Mission-aligned and adaptable. You're enthusiastic about CDI's mission and comfortable operating in an environment of continuous improvement as the LI program evolves year to year.

  • Preferred: Comfort with project management systems and CRMs (e.g., Asana, HubSpot).

Benefits

  • Compensation — $85,000 - $95,000 annually

  • A Mission-Driven Culture — our work culture genuinely reflects our mission, characterized by intellectual humility, continuous improvement, and open-mindedness

  • Remote-First — CDI was founded as a remote-first organization, and we work hard to maintain a strong team culture across vast distances

  • Unlimited PTO — as well as 13 company holidays

  • Remote Work Support — up to $500 reimbursed for home office equipment (like desks, chairs, or webcams) and up to $50/month reimbursed for home internet or cell phone expenses

  • Other Benefits — employer-supported health, vision and dental plans, subsidized parental leave, 3% 401k match, short- and long-term disability insurance, life and AD&D insurance, $1,000 annual professional development budget

Role Specs

  • Reports to: Vice President of Leadership Programs

  • Schedule: Full-time, flexible within U.S. time zones

  • Target start date: ASAP

  • Location: Remote, must be based in the U.S.

Highlights

CDI seeks a Senior Program Manager to serve as the operational backbone of the Leadership Institute, equipping senior higher ed leaders with strategy, tools, and peer networks for dialogue.

Interns will also have the opportunity to present their project work to company leaders, network with executives, and participate in educational programs designed to support their personal and professional growth. Additionally, interns will engage in community service projects and social events, building connections with fellow interns and the broader American Equity team.

The internship will be a 12 week program located at our downtown Des Moines office.

GENERAL PURPOSE OF THE JOB:

American Equity’s Summer Internship Program is designed to provide Actuarial students with an immersive, challenging, and meaningful real-world work experience that replicates as closely as possible the career journey of an American Equity actuarial associate. The Actuarial Intern works on a team with responsibility for one of the primary actuarial functions including modeling, pricing, valuation and reporting of deferred annuities including but not limited to fixed indexed annuities. Each intern is assigned an impactful project to support company initiatives.

**Position is based in Des Moines, IA with an on-site working schedule**

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Each intern project may include any of these listed duties and responsibilities:

  • Model development in Milliman’s Integrate modeling software for fixed indexed annuities including identifying, addressing and resolving model changes in a controlled framework.
  • Ensuring the accuracy of the calculations and inputs in Integrate model using Excel-based independent calculators.
  • Generating and reviewing reserve calculations across both Statutory and GAAP reporting requirements on fixed indexed annuities.
  • Reporting, validating and analyzing current assets and liabilities, as well as delivering required quarterly reporting items.
  • Building reports in Integrate for fixed indexed annuities or similar products for additional management analysis.
  • Assisting in product design and developing actuarial models to competitively and profitably price new liabilities.
  • Assisting in rate setting for new or existing annuity products.
  • Supporting the validation of contract values for other departments.
  • Modifying and enhancing independent policy calculators.
  • Researching policyholder data using various tools such as SQL, R, Python, and Tableau.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES:

None.

EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE:

  • Actively pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in actuarial science, data science, or related field of study.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, PROFESSIONAL DESIGNATIONS:

  • Passing score on at least 1 preliminary actuarial examination is required.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including ability to research and analyze data with little instruction.
  • Strong preference of being self-motivated and results oriented.
  • Exceptional attention to numeric and other details.
  • Effective organization skills.
  • Effective verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to work collaboratively and successfully with coworkers, vendors, and other outside third parties.
  • Ability to successfully handle pressure and meet deadlines in a face-paced work environment.
  • Demonstrated commitment to continuous learning and development.

title: Senior Full-Stack (Java/React)
description:

Opportunity for impact

Newfire Global Partners, a leader in developing disruptive healthcare technology, collaborates with Fortune 500 companies and start-ups to drive transformation.

Newfire is seeking a Senior Full-Stack (Java/React)

What's the Project?
Our client is a well-established company in the luxury retail industry undergoing a major technology transformation. They have chosen Newfire as their long-term engineering partner for their digital ecosystem: a large custom e-commerce platform, multiple online storefronts, and ERP integrations. The goal is to modernize the platform and speed up software delivery, taking release cycles from several months down to about one.

We're building a team of experienced engineers who enjoy solving hard technical problems, improving large production systems, and working through real-world technical debt. This is not a greenfield project; it's a chance to make a real impact on the reliability, scalability, and delivery speed of a platform the business runs on. Development here is AI-native, with agentic development tools like Claude Code and CodeRabbit available, and part of every engineer's job is making the codebase work well for this way of working.




  • Shipping customer-facing features behind feature flags, in small reviewed PRs
  • Improving the code you touch: decomposing oversized services, adding tests, migrating backend code toward Java 21 / Spring Boot 3.x

  • Documenting what you learn and decide

Please note that employment will be contingent upon providing documentation verifying your legal work authorization in the country of residence, in accordance with applicable law.


  • 6+ years of commercial software engineering, genuinely full-stack (not 90/10 one way)
  • Strong Java and Spring Boot, including JPA/Hibernate, database migrations (Flyway or similar), and relational data modeling
  • Strong React and TypeScript with modern Next.js (App Router, Server Components, current data-fetching patterns)
  • Solid PostgreSQL
  • Experience modernizing or maintaining a large existing codebase in production
  • Full ownership of what you ship, including testing: unit, integration, and E2E
  • Shared-codebase discipline: trunk-based development, small frequent PRs, feature flags, respect for module boundaries
  • Fluency with AI-assisted, agentic development: coding agents such as Claude Code, context engineering, AI code review and test generation
  • Good security hygiene: no secrets in code, careful input handling, changes through reviewed PRs and CI
  • Solid REST API design and experience integrating third-party services
  • Familiarity with Agile/Scrum practices
  • Proactive communication; you surface problems early and write things down
  • Excellent spoken and written English
  • Significant US Eastern Time overlap (we staff from our LATAM and EMEA delivery hubs)

title: Remote B2B Telephone Interviewer
description:
Work from anywhere in the UK | £14.27 per hour* (£15.99 incl holiday pay)
Full or part-time
Daytime shifts available

Spaces are limited,we encourage early applications as this role will close once we receive sufficient applications.

Are you looking for a role that fits around your life?

Do you want to build confidence, learn new skills and work on projects that make a real difference to society?

We’re increasing our remote B2B interviewing team and are looking for friendly, reliable people to join us. You’ll be helping us deliver important research projects for government agencies and organisations – all from the comfort of your own home.

About us

IFF is an award-winning social research agency, that helps organisations, businesses and individuals to make better informed decisions. We deliver best-in-class social research on topics that really matter, helping shape public policy and informing programmes and initiatives that make a difference to people’s lives.

Our values:

  • Human first – we understand life happens and offer flexibility

  • Independent & impartial – we let the evidence do the talking

  • Making a difference – through the projects we take on and how we work

About the role

You’ll be working from home, carrying out high-quality telephone interviews on behalf of our research team. You’ll follow a guided script and recording responses accurately, for example, callingbusiness owners and senior decision-makers, to help the UK Government assist employers by better understanding needs in terms of skills, training, and employment.

This isn’t cold calling, it’s important work to capture information and support research, you’ll need to show confidence, build rapport, listen carefully, ask questions and capture answers.

This is a fully remote role. You’ll need a computer/laptop, a USB headset and an Ethernet connection.

This is a UK based role and you must be able to work from a UK location.

Shifts available:

Once you’ve completed your paid training, you can book shifts weekly:

  • Daytime: Mon–Fri 9am to 4.30pm (or shorter shifts available).

Pick shifts on our booking portal that work for you; there will be an abundance of shifts; it's about selecting ones to suit your earning needs and lifestyle.

About you

  • Great people skills – you enjoy speaking to a variety of people

  • Confident using a computer and noting down information accurately

  • Reliable and able to work towards targets

  • Ideally, some phone-based experience (customer service, sales or similar), but not required as full training provided

  • A quiet home working space and broadband connection

What’s in it for you?

  • Flexible shifts – full or short daytime shifts to suit your schedule

  • Work from anywhere in the UK

  • Above Real Living Wage – £14.27 per hour + holiday pay (£15.99 + bonuses) after training

  • Full training & daily support – we set you up for success

  • Achievable bonuses

  • A friendly, supportive team culture – plus social activities & wellbeing resources

What's next?
You’ll need to complete our application form, which includes six key criteria that must be met (these are knockout questions, and you won’t progress if you don’t meet them).

You’ll answer additional questions to help us understand your experience and preferred ways of working, followed by a short diversity monitoring form.

You’ll then be sent a link to our virtual video assessment, which focuses on your customer service and telephone skills. We’ll make our decision based on these outcomes.
If you're successful at this stage you'll be invited for a paid live trial training session.

*please note: Your live trial and training period will be paid at our training rate of £12.71 plus holiday. If you successfully pass the training period you'll be paid at the hourly rate of £14.27 plus holiday.

JOB OVERVIEW

MartinFed is seeking an experienced Senior SailPoint Subject Matter Expert (SME) to provide technical leadership, architecture, development, and operational oversight for an enterprise on-premises SailPoint environment supporting a federal customer.

The Senior SailPoint SME will serve as the technical authority for the SailPoint platform, with responsibility for overall system architecture, application performance, code quality, workflow design, integrations, connectors, data correlation, and daily SailPoint operations. This individual will also lead and mentor junior SailPoint engineers supporting the DevOps team and provide advanced technical support for issues escalated from the Helpdesk.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

  • Serve as the Senior SailPoint SME and technical lead for the customer's on-premises SailPoint environment.
  • Design and architect the overall SailPoint solution to ensure scalability, reliability, security, efficiency, and performance.
  • Provide architectural oversight and recommendations related to SailPoint infrastructure, configurations, integrations, and platform strategy.

  • Establish and enforce code review and validation practices, ensuring changes are independently tested and reviewed prior to incorporation into the production codebase.
  • Provide design oversight for SailPoint workflows supporting internal and external account management functions.
  • Design and review identity lifecycle processes, provisioning workflows, approval processes, access requests, and account management functionality.
  • Oversee SailPoint daily processes, scheduled tasks, aggregations, connectors, and integrations.
  • Monitor and troubleshoot identity synchronization, aggregation, provisioning, and data correlation issues, ensuring problems are quickly identified and resolved.
  • Troubleshoot complex SailPoint application, connector, workflow, integration, and performance issues.
  • Evaluate new SailPoint product features and releases and provide recommendations to Government PMs regarding their applicability, value, risks, and potential implementation.
  • Provide technical recommendations to Government leadership regarding SailPoint architecture and design strategy decisions.
  • Lead, mentor, and provide technical guidance to junior SailPoint engineers supporting the DevOps team.
  • Review junior engineers' designs, configurations, troubleshooting approaches, and code to ensure technical quality and adherence to established standards.
  • Support DevOps processes related to SailPoint development, testing, deployment, configuration management, and release management.
  • Assist with complex helpdesk tickets escalated to the DevOps engineering team.
  • Perform root cause analysis and develop long-term solutions for recurring SailPoint and identity management issues.
  • Develop and maintain technical documentation, architecture diagrams, configuration documentation, troubleshooting procedures, and operational guidance.
  • Collaborate with Government stakeholders, system administrators, developers, security teams, and other technical SMEs to support the overall Identity and Access Management (IAM) environment.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • United States Citizen with a DoD Secret clearance.
  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Project Management, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related discipline; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.
  • 10+ years of hands-on experience developing code for and maintaining on-premises SailPoint installations.
  • Extensive experience with SailPoint IdentityIQ (IIQ) architecture, development, configuration, administration, and maintenance.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and architecting enterprise SailPoint solutions.
  • Strong SailPoint development experience, including customization of workflows, rules, connectors, integrations, and identity lifecycle processes.
  • Experience with Java and BeanShell development within SailPoint environments.
  • Experience with SailPoint provisioning, aggregation, identity correlation, access requests, certifications, and account lifecycle management.
  • Experience developing, configuring, and troubleshooting SailPoint connectors and integrations with enterprise applications and directories.
  • Strong understanding of identity lifecycle management, including Joiner/Mover/Leaver (JML) processes.
  • Experience troubleshooting synchronization, aggregation, correlation, and provisioning failures.
  • Experience with relational databases and supporting database technologies used within SailPoint environments.
  • Experience implementing source control, code review, testing, and release management practices.
  • Experience troubleshooting complex production issues in enterprise IAM environments.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead and mentor junior engineers.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate complex technical concepts to Government stakeholders and technical teams.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain any Government clearance, suitability determination, or facility access required for the position.

DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Experience supporting SailPoint IdentityIQ within a federal Government environment.
  • Experience leading or serving as a senior technical SME for a large-scale enterprise IAM program.
  • Experience integrating SailPoint with technologies such as Active Directory, LDAP, databases, web services/APIs, and enterprise applications.
  • Experience with REST/SOAP APIs and custom connector development.
  • Knowledge of RBAC, ABAC, least privilege, access governance, privileged access, and Zero Trust principles.

title: Hygienist - GA East Cobb Monday to Thursday ($500 Sign on)
description:
JOB PURPOSE

Registered Dental Hygienists are assigned duties and responsibilities which involve licensed professional work providing dental hygiene services. A Registered Dental Hygienist (RDH) implements appropriate standard of care therapy, assists a dentist in providing hygiene, periodontal or dental care and treatment, provides dental hygiene assessments, creates treatment plans based on a dentist's diagnosis, and provides oral and overall health care education and instruction to patients.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

•Assess patients' teeth, bone, and periodontal tissues indicating the presence of any abnormalities or suspected diseases or conditions.

•Creates periodontal treatment plans based on the dentist's diagnosis.

•Bring to the immediate attention of the dentist any suspected lesion in the mouth or on the teeth.

•Thoroughly remove soft and hard deposits and extrinsic stain from teeth, using hand instruments, ultrasonic cavitron inserts, and prophy handpieces.

•Instruct patients on good oral hygiene practices, recommend appropriate products or devices for patients' home care, and provide other health care education, as necessary.

•Perform prophylaxis in the absence of periodontal disease or gingivitis.

•Perform full mouth debridement, either as a first stage gingivitis therapy or to remove interfering calculus to further enable a more accurate diagnosis and treatment plan.

•Perform scaling and root planing as a periodontal therapy.

•Place locally administered antibiotics as supportive periodontal therapy.

•Implement irrigation and desensitizing procedures or products as adjunctive to periodontal therapy.

•Position and expose dental and carpal radiographic film and sensors.

•Perform in-office whitening procedures, including first application of gel, curing the gel, and subsequent applications.

•Apply cavity-preventive agents, such as fluorides and pit and fissure sealants.

•Make recommendations as to patients' re-care interval and follow-up needs.

•All other duties and responsibilities as assigned and allowed under applicable Florida state laws and regulations.

QUALIFICATIONS

•Must be licensed and in good standing with the state of Georgia.

•Associates or Bachelor's degree in dental hygiene.

•Current Basic Life Support (BLS) and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) certificate.

•Must be willing to partner with the dentist and work well as a member of the total dental team. Should have visual acuity and manual dexterity, since they use dental instruments within a patient's mouth with little room for error.

WORKING CONDITIONS

An RDH works in clean, well-lit offices. Important health safeguards include, but are not limited to strict adherence to proper radiological procedures, infection control protocols, and the use of appropriate personal protective equipment when administering anesthetic gas, handling or using cleaning chemicals, or working in the dental laboratory.

An RDH must also wear appropriate personal protective equipment including, at minimum, safety glasses, surgical masks, full arm length gowns/lab coats, and gloves to protect themselves and patients from infectious diseases during all patient care and when handling contaminated instruments or equipment. Open-toe shoes are forbidden, long hair must be pulled back, and fingernails must be kept short and tidy.

title: DevSecOps Engineer
description:
We are looking for a security-focused DevSecOps Engineer with 1-2 years of experience to help embed security across the software development lifecycle while maintaining deployment speed, platform reliability, and compliance.

This role will work closely with engineering, infrastructure, and security teams to strengthen CI/CD security, cloud governance, infrastructure automation, vulnerability management, monitoring, and secure deployment practices.

Roles and Responsibilities

Secure DevOps & CI/CD

  • Build, maintain, and optimize secure CI/CD pipelines for reliability, speed, and controlled releases.
  • Implement shift-left security by integrating security checks early in the development lifecycle.
  • Configure automated quality, vulnerability, and security gates within release pipelines.
  • Support secure, zero-downtime deployment strategies and rollback mechanisms.
  • Ensure release workflows follow secure SDLC and change-management practices.

Cloud and Infrastructure Security

  • Manage and secure cloud environments across AWS, GCP, or Azure.
  • Develop and maintain Infrastructure-as-Code using Terraform.
  • Package and deploy applications to Kubernetes using Helm.
  • Implement cloud security controls, including IAM policies, least-privilege access, network segmentation, and secure configuration management.
  • Strengthen Docker and Kubernetes security, including image hardening, access controls, and workload protection.

Application and Platform Security

  • Integrate SAST, DAST, SCA, container scanning, and vulnerability assessment tools into CI/CD pipelines.
  • Track vulnerabilities, coordinate remediation, and ensure closure within defined timelines.
  • Implement secure secrets management, certificate management, and encryption practices.
  • Participate in application, infrastructure, and architecture security reviews.
  • Support security testing and remediation across applications and platforms.

Compliance, Monitoring and Incident Readiness

  • Support compliance with frameworks such as ISO 27001, SOC 2, PCI-DSS, and other regulatory requirements.
  • Maintain centralized security logging, monitoring, alerting, and audit trails.
  • Track security posture, vulnerabilities, access reviews, and compliance metrics.
  • Support incident response readiness, security investigations, and remediation activities.
  • Maintain documentation required for audits, risk assessments, and compliance reviews.

Automation and Reliability

  • Automate repetitive infrastructure, deployment, and security processes.
  • Improve observability through effective logging, monitoring, alerting, and dashboards.
  • Support disaster recovery, backup validation, resilience testing, and business continuity initiatives.
  • Collaborate with SRE and platform teams to improve availability, scalability, and operational security.

Required Qualifications

  • 1-2 years of experience in DevSecOps, DevOps, Cloud Security, SRE, or a related role.
  • Hands-on experience with at least one cloud platform: AWS, GCP, or Azure.
  • Strong working knowledge of Terraform for Infrastructure-as-Code.
  • Hands-on experience with Kubernetes, Docker, and Helm.
  • Experience with CI/CD tools such as Jenkins, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Azure DevOps, or similar platforms.
  • Practical understanding of DevSecOps, secure SDLC, vulnerability management, and security automation.
  • Experience integrating or working with SAST, DAST, SCA, container scanning, or vulnerability management tools.
  • Understanding of IAM, least-privilege access, network security, secrets management, and encryption.
  • Proficiency in at least one scripting or programming language, such as Python, Go, or Bash.
  • Ability to collaborate with engineering teams and drive timely closure of security issues.

Good to Have

  • AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, CKA, or CKAD certification.
  • Exposure to ISO 27001, SOC 2, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, or similar compliance frameworks.
  • Experience working in healthcare, fintech, or another regulated industry.
  • Familiarity with SIEM, CSPM, WAF, cloud-native security tools, and incident-response processes.
  • Experience with tools such as SonarQube, Snyk, Trivy, Checkmarx, Veracode, OWASP ZAP, or similar platforms.

Application review → introductory conversation → hiring manager interview → offer.

description:
Job Summary

The Senior Quality Engineer is responsible for documenting and analyzing quality assurance procedures and may be responsible for quality control testing of final products. The Senior Quality Engineer designs, implements and tests Quality Assurance process sampling systems, procedures and statistical techniques to make certain products fulfill both specified quality standards and safety regulations. The Senior Quality Engineer must be proficient in technical writing. The Senior Quality Engineer works within a team of other Quality Assurance professionals. Work assignments are given by the Quality Manager.

Essential Functions

  • Formulates Quality Assurance policies and procedures for the Quality Management System.
  • Regularly exercises independent judgment and discretion about matters of significance.
  • Maintains Quality Management System.
  • Provides technical assistance and definition of inspection and test criteria to Quality Control personnel.
  • Works with Engineering and other departments to determine Quality Assurance Requirements for new and existing products.
  • Establishes statistical confidence by identifying sample size and acceptable error, determines levels of confidence.
  • Provides technical, reporting and analytical expertise in evaluating warranty and non-warranty repairs and oversees the Return Material Authorization (RMA) process.
  • Serves as a senior member of the Management Review Board (MRB).
  • Completes nonconformance control including disposition, failure analysis, trending, and corrective action.
  • Prepares defect analysis reports by collecting, analyzing, and summarizing data and making recommendations for improvement.
  • Determines areas for quality improvement by identifying and pursuing improvement methodology relevant to manufacturing processes.
  • Works with the Supply Chain department to ensure continued quality of incoming parts through regular audits and ratings of the supply base, including corrective action where appropriate.
  • Ensures that new vendors meet the requirements of the QMS.
  • Maintains safe and healthy work environment by following standards and procedures, complying with legal regulations.

  • Ensure weights and capacity of outbound loads are correct and work with the warehouse team to adjust as necessary.
  • Implement and monitor performance metrics for transportation and work with management team to enhance improvement of processes.

Dispatch

title: Freelance Software Engineer - AI Coding Agent Evaluation
description:
Please submit your CV in English and indicate your level of English proficiency.

Mindrift connects specialists with project-based AI opportunities for leading tech companies, focused on testing, evaluating, and improving AI systems. Participation is project-based, not permanent employment.

About the Role

You’ll design coding tasks that challenge frontier AI coding agents. Each task is a self-contained Docker environment with a broken piece of software; an AI agent attempts the fix; automated tests verify the outcome. Your deliverable is the full task package: broken code, tests, instructions, and a reference solution proving the task is solvable.

Responsibilities:

  • Invent a realistic developer scenario — a real bug, a broken ETL, a missing feature — not a toy problem.
  • Build a reproducible Docker environment with pinned dependencies.
  • Write a pytest that verifies outcomes, not specific commands — deterministic, non-flaky, and does not leak the fix.
  • Write an instruction.md that reads like a Jira ticket a developer would receive.
  • Write a reference solve.sh proving the task is solvable.
  • Calibrate difficulty so current state-of-the-art agents solve the task 20–60% of the time.
  • Iterate based on feedback from expert QA reviewers.
  • Later: review other authors’ tasks as a QA reviewer.

Not in scope

  • Data labeling, prompt engineering.
  • Production code to ship — you design problems and verification for AI agents.
  • Leetcode puzzles — scenarios must look like real developer work.
  • Not every candidate task ships — quality over quantity.

Requirements

  • 3+ years of production software development in one backend stack — Python, Go, Node.js, Java, or Rust. Depth in one stack beats breadth.
  • Python + pytest fluency — required regardless of primary stack. The task harness is pytest-based even when the broken app is in another language. Fixtures, parametrize, monkeypatch, timeouts, conftest.py.
  • Docker authoring — reproducible Dockerfiles, pinned dependencies, multi-stage builds when needed, non-root user.
  • Linux & Bash — comfort debugging inside containers (strace, lsof, journalctl); shell beyond set -euo pipefail.
  • AI coding agent experience — Claude Code, Cursor, Roo Code, or similar, on non-trivial work. You can cite a specific time the AI was confidently wrong and how you caught it.
  • English — B2+ written.

Not a fit

  • Data Science, ML, or Computer Vision engineers without backend-engineering output.
  • Manual QA testers without automation or test authoring.
  • Frontend-only, low-code / no-code, IT Support, or Business Analysts.
  • Engineers who have never written pytest from scratch.
  • Junior, intern, or assistant as the most recent role.

Preferred qualifications

  • Domain depth in Security, System Administration (nginx / systemd / cron), Scientific Computing (NumPy / PyTorch / SciPy), DevOps, or Git internals.
  • Modern Python tooling (uv, poetry, pyproject.toml).
  • Coverage tooling (pytest-cov, coverage.py, gcov, llvm-cov, kcov).
  • Fuzzing or property-based testing (Hypothesis).
  • Prior contribution to agent-evaluation benchmarks or related frameworks.

Process

Apply → Pass qualification (90-minute sample-task screen + short behavioral interview) → Join a project → Complete tasks → Get paid.

Time commitment

  • Onboarding: ~10 hours per first task.
  • Steady state: ~5 hours per task, 2–4 parallel tasks per author.
  • Realistic weekly load: 8–20 hours. Higher volume available for top performers.
  • You choose when and how to contribute; tasks must be submitted by the deadline and meet acceptance criteria.

Compensation:

  • Paid contributions, rates up to $35/hour*.
  • Task-based compensation equivalent to hourly rate, depending on performance and volume.
  • Some projects include incentive payments.

*Rates vary based on expertise, skills assessment, location, project needs, and other factors. Higher rates may be provided to highly specialized experts. Lower rates may apply during onboarding or non-core project phases. Payment details are shared per project.

Apply

Submit your CV via the Mindrift platform. Indicate your English level, note this role (Software Engineering Evaluation Specialist — Terminal Bench), and include a GitHub profile link if available.

title: Manufacturing Parts Coordinator - Night Shift
description:
This is a 12-hour rotating night shift

About the Role

As a Parts Coordinator, you will play a critical role in ensuring our plant operates efficiently by managing the day-to-day operation of the parts storeroom. Your primary focus will be ensuring the right parts and materials are available when needed, minimizing downtime and supporting the successful execution of the plant's maintenance plan.

Working closely with Maintenance, Production, and Scheduling teams, you'll manage inventory levels, coordinate parts procurement, and maintain accurate inventory data within SAP. This position is crucial in helping the plant achieve its operational, reliability, and customer service goals.

What You'll Do

  • Manage the purchasing, receiving, and stocking of repair parts and operating supplies to support plant operations.
  • Maintain optimal spare parts inventory levels, balancing working capital requirements with operational reliability.
  • Ensure critical parts are available to prevent unplanned downtime and production interruptions.
  • Operate and maintain an organized, efficient storeroom that provides excellent service to Maintenance, Production, and Scheduling teams.
  • Partner with the Maintenance Planner to coordinate parts ordering and deliveries in line with scheduled maintenance activities.
  • Prioritize parts requirements to support urgent maintenance needs and reduce equipment downtime.
  • Identify opportunities to control costs through effective planning, inventory management, alternative sourcing, and supplier relationships.
  • Create and maintain parts records within SAP, ensuring accurate material requirements planning (MRP) data, classifications, and metadata.
  • Maintain the integrity and accuracy of inventory records and the CMMS database.
  • Collaborate closely with mechanics and other plant personnel to source and support parts requirements for maintenance and project activities.

About You

We're looking for someone who is organized, detail-oriented, and thrives in a fast-paced manufacturing environment. You take ownership of your responsibilities, enjoy solving problems, and are committed to delivering results.

Qualifications & Experience

  • High School Diploma or GED required.
  • 1–2 years of inventory management, maintenance planning support, or storeroom experience required.
  • Experience using a Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS), preferably SAP.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining accuracy and efficiency.
  • Comfortable working cross-functionally with Maintenance, Production, and Supply Chain teams.
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs. and lift heavier items with appropriate assistance.

What Makes You Successful

  • You take ownership and follow through on commitments.
  • You enjoy working in a fast-paced, hands-on manufacturing environment.
  • You are proactive, resourceful, and focused on continuous improvement.
  • You balance attention to detail with a strong sense of urgency.

description:

title: Digital Patient Experience Architect
description:
AnewHealth is one of the nation’s leading pharmacy care management companies that specializes in caring for people with the most complex, chronic needs—wherever they call home. We enable better outcomes for patients and the healthcare organizations who support them. Established in 2023 through the combination of ExactCare and Tabula Rasa HealthCare, we provide a suite of solutions that includes comprehensive pharmacy services; full-service pharmacy benefit management; and specialized support services for Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly. With over 1,400 team members, we care for more than 100,000 people across all 50 states.

Job Details

The Digital Patient Experience Architect will own the enterprise solution identification, roadmap, implementation, and adoption of AnewHealth’s patient-facing digital engagement ecosystem. The role will focus on reducing patient friction, improving digital adoption, increasing early patient confidence, supporting packet completeness and readiness, reducing avoidable contacts, and enabling a more proactive Health Navigator experience.

The Digital Patient Experience Architect will translate enterprise patient experience standards, journey requirements, and communications governance into digital requirements, product priorities, workflow design, launch readiness criteria, and post-launch performance management.

Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain the digital patient experience roadmap, prioritizing initiatives that improve adoption, reduce friction, increase self-service completion, support early patient confidence, and drive measurable outcomes across referral/conversion, start of care, engagement center, medication readiness, refill readiness, and ongoing retention.

  • Translate journey enablement playbooks, service recovery standards, and approved patient communications requirements into digital channel requirements, workflow logic, launch readiness criteria, and post-launch optimization plans.

  • Serve as the enterprise owner for digital touchpoint performance, including adoption, engagement, completion, drop-off, escalation rate, avoidable contact reduction, digital containment, time-to-fix, and patient confidence indicators.

  • Lead the transformation of the digital front door experience, ensuring patients have a clear, guided, and confidence-building path from initial outreach through education, activation, account creation, medication confirmation, and next-step completion.

  • Own the digital enablement strategy for the Health Navigator experience, including guided workflows that support packet completeness, missing information resolution, packet readiness, readiness gates, progress visibility, escalation triggers, and appropriate human handoffs.

  • Partners with Patient Experience Design & Delivery, Product, IT, Operations, Growth, Compliance, Legal, Telecoms, Patient Insights & Analytics, and AI/automation vendors to ensure digital touchpoints are coordinated, measurable, and continuously improved.

  • Lead continuous improvement routines for digital engagement performance, including monitoring friction signals, identifying root causes, recommending prioritized fixes, coordinating resolution with accountable teams, and measuring whether changes improved patient experience and operational performance

  • Own the performance and optimization strategy for AI-enabled patient engagement capabilities.

  • Define and maintain digital readiness standards for major operational, product, policy, and technology changes that impact patients, including digital launch readiness, channel monitoring, workflow validation, and post-launch performance review.

  • Identify digital experience gaps that create avoidable contacts, escalations, readiness delays, medication completeness issues, or patient confusion, and create prioritized improvement plans with clear owners, expected impact, and measurable success criteria

  • Create executive-level reporting and narratives that connect digital engagement performance to enterprise outcomes, including patient trust, retention, UE savings, avoidable contact reduction, medication completeness, packet readiness, digital adoption, and operational scalability.

  • Embody AnewHealth’s Core Values in all communications and interactions.

  • Other duties as assigned.

The above essential functions are representative of major duties of positions in this job classification. Specific duties and responsibilities may vary based upon departmental needs. Other duties may be assigned similar to the above consistent with knowledge, skills and abilities required for the job. Not all of the duties may be assigned to a position.

Qualifications: These represent the desired qualifications of the ideal candidate. They are not meant to limit consideration for candidates who do not meet all of the standards listed. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Product Management, Digital Experience, Healthcare Administration, Business, Marketing, Communications, Human-Computer Interaction, Information Systems, or related field.

  • Master’s or PharmD degree preferred.

Experience

  • Required: 6+ years of progressive experience in digital engagement, digital product management, patient/customer experience, healthcare technology, digital transformation, or related fields.

  • Required: Experience developing roadmaps, defining business and user requirements, prioritizing digital improvements, and partnering with Product/IT teams through launch and post-launch optimization.

  • Required: Experience leading cross-functional initiatives with Product, IT, Operations, Compliance, Legal, Analytics, Telecoms, Growth, and/or business stakeholders.

  • Required: Experience using engagement data to identify friction, improve adoption, reduce avoidable contacts, and measure performance against defined outcomes.

  • Preferred: Healthcare experience, including pharmacy, payer, provider, care delivery, patient access, patient onboarding, medication management, contact center, or digital health experience.

  • Preferred: Experience with AI-enabled engagement solutions and omnichannel orchestration.

  • Preferred: Experience improving operational outcomes through digital engagement, including adoption improvement, contact deflection, workflow automation, or readiness optimization.

Skills & Abilities

  • Required: Strong digital strategy and product-thinking skills, with the ability to translate patient needs, journey requirements, and enterprise priorities into actionable roadmaps and measurable outcomes.

  • Required: Demonstrated ability to lead complex, cross-functional initiatives in a matrixed environment without relying solely on direct authority.

  • Required: Strong understanding of patient journey design, digital adoption, friction reduction, and how digital engagement impacts trust, retention, operational efficiency, and patient confidence.

  • Required: Ability to define digital engagement KPIs, interpret performance data, identify root causes, and convert insights into prioritized improvement plans.

  • Required: Strong executive communication and storytelling skills, including the ability to clearly articulate risks, tradeoffs, recommendations, expected impact, and performance outcomes.

  • Required: Strong project and roadmap leadership skills, including requirements definition, dependency tracking, issue escalation, launch readiness, adoption planning, and post-launch monitoring.

  • Required: Strong judgment in regulated environments, including comfort partnering with Compliance and Legal on patient-facing workflows, digital outreach, consent language, AI-enabled interactions, and service recovery use cases.

  • Required: Ability to partner effectively with Product and IT to translate digital patient experience needs into user stories, workflow requirements, instrumentation needs, and release priorities.

  • Preferred: Familiarity with Microsoft 365, Power Platform, CRM tools, SMS/email platforms, contact center platforms, patient portals, app analytics, product analytics, chat platforms, and AI/automation vendor solutions.

  • Preferred: Strong understanding of healthcare operations, medication management workflows, patient onboarding, refill readiness, start-of-care processes, and service recovery.

Schedule: This is a full-time position with an expectation to work an average of 40 hours per week and be available outside of normal business hours to meet customer expectations on an ad-hoc basis. Schedules are set to accommodate the requirements of the position and the needs of the organization and may be adjusted as needed. This may be considered a remote position based on manager discretion.

Travel: Travel may be required for special organization or department events, department team meetings, trade shows, conferences, and other client engagements.

Supervisory: No. May provide day-to-day direction to contractors or dotted-line resources as the function scales.

This is a remote position.

AnewHealth offers a comprehensive benefit package for full-time employees that includes medical/dental/vision, flexible spending, company-paid life insurance and short-term disability as well as voluntary benefits, 401(k), Paid Time Off and paid holidays. Medical, dental and vision coverage are effective 1st of the month following date of hire.

AnewHealth provides equal employment opportunity to all qualified applicants regardless of race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, or veteran status, or other legally protected classification in the state in which a person is seeking employment. Applicants are encouraged to confidentially self-identify when applying. Local applicants are encouraged to apply. We maintain a drug-free work environment. Applicants must be eligible to work in this country.

About CDI

The Constructive Dialogue Institute (CDI) is a non-partisan, non-profit dedicated to equipping the next generation of Americans with the skills to communicate and collaborate across lines of difference. We work with U.S. colleges and universities by providing co-curricular programming for students, professional development for faculty and staff, and strategic guidance to leadership. Our goal is to foster constructive dialogue at every level of the institution and to create the conditions for lasting organizational change. CDI was co-founded by psychologist Jonathan Haidt, the bestselling author of The Righteous Mind and The Anxious Generation.

About the Role

CDI is seeking a strategic, media-savvy communicator to serve as Vice President of Strategic Communications. Reporting to the Chief Growth Officer, the VP will be responsible for establishing CDI as the leading national voice on constructive dialogue in higher education and converting that visibility into audience growth and organizational credibility.

This is a hands-on builder role. The VP will lead CDI's communications strategy, earned media, executive profile-building, messaging and narrative, editorial leadership of CDI's thought leadership and newsletter, organic social, and crisis and reputation management. Initially, the VP will operate as an individual contributor supported by fractional and contractor resources. Over time, the VP will manage a Communications & Content Manager, who will serve as the editorial and production engine for owned content.

The ideal candidate brings 10–12 years of experience in strategic communications, strong relationships across national and higher education media, and a track record of building organizational reputation in complex, high-stakes environments.

Responsibilities

Lead CDI's communications strategy and narrative

  • Set the annual communications and thought leadership strategy, defining editorial priorities and narrative direction in service of CDI's mission and earned revenue goals.

  • Serve as a trusted communications advisor to the Executive Director and Chief Growth Officer, helping assess trade-offs, evaluate reputational risk, and align leadership on key messaging decisions before work advances.

  • Own CDI's messaging guide and narrative framework, ensuring consistent, politically grounded communication across all external channels.

  • Monitor CDI's reputational landscape — including dynamics around partners, founders, and key stakeholders — alongside political, cultural, and higher education trends, to proactively identify risks and opportunities and advise leadership.

Elevate CDI's executive and thought leadership profile

  • Lead CDI's executive visibility program, building the Executive Director and other key CDI figures' profiles through op-eds, podcast appearances, conference keynotes, and media placements, and preparing and coaching the Executive Director for public appearances and interviews.

  • Partner with CDI's thought-leadership bench (across the Research, Education, Culture Change teams) to translate research findings into media-ready narratives and public-facing content.

Build and own CDI's earned media presence

  • Drive proactive media outreach to national, higher education, and mission-aligned press; build and maintain relationships with journalists, editors, and influencers.

  • Lead rapid response and crisis communications, managing reputational risk with speed and sound judgment.

Lead owned media and editorial

  • Provide editorial leadership for CDI's higher education newsletter and blog; manage the Communications & Content Manager to maintain publishing cadence and quality.

  • Own organic social strategy (brand, executive, and thought-leadership content), with the Communications & Content Manager executing the unified calendar.

  • Coordinate the thought-leadership editorial calendar with the Impact team, Partnerships, and the thought-leadership bench.

Support external relationships and cross-functional work

  • Support CDI's broader external relationships — including with funders, board members, and senior institutional partners — by ensuring CDI's communications reflect the organization's impact, credibility, and strategic direction.

  • Partner with the Senior Manager of Demand Generation to connect comms outputs — earned media, newsletter audience, thought leadership — to Marketing Qualified Pipeline, ensuring visibility translates into partnerships opportunities and earned revenue.

Build and lead the communications team

  • Manage the Communications & Content Manager, providing editorial direction, coaching, and prioritization.

  • Establish the communications operating model: workflows, editorial planning system, brand standards, and cross-functional feedback loops.

  • Define and track the communications scorecard: 25 earned placements and 100 mentions annually; 30% year-over-year audience growth across the HE newsletter and LinkedIn; two research studies each yielding at least one feature placement.

Requirements

About You

  • Senior communications leader: 10–12 years of experience in strategic communications, or PR, with demonstrated success building organizational reputation and growing audiences in complex, politically sensitive environments.

  • Media relationships: Established connections across national, higher education, and mission-aligned press; track record of securing high-quality placements.

  • Exceptional judgment: Deep instinct for when to engage — CDI's credibility depends on nonpartisan restraint as much as visibility. Proven track record protecting organizational reputation in politically sensitive environments while proactively shaping a positive organizational narrative, with the ability to clearly articulate trade-offs and advise leadership on risk.

  • Strong writer and editor: Track record producing or overseeing high-quality long-form thought leadership and executive communications.

  • Hands-on operator: Comfortable executing with speed, rigor, and attention to detail while building for scale; in a small organization, VP-level execution and follow-through are as important as vision.

  • Builder mindset: Experience establishing or significantly evolving a communications function, including processes, standards, and team structure; experience managing people in a startup or scaling organization.

  • Cross-functional collaborator: Proven ability to coordinate editorial and campaign work across research, marketing, and partnerships teams, and to align leadership before advancing work.

  • Mission-aligned: Deeply motivated by CDI's mission, with the political awareness to communicate constructively and credibly across ideological lines. Familiarity with the higher education landscape strongly preferred.

Benefits

  • Compensation —$175,000-$195,000 (based on experience)

  • A Mission-Driven Culture — our work culture genuinely reflects our mission, characterized by intellectual humility, continuous improvement, and open-mindedness

  • Remote-First — CDI was founded as a remote-first organization, and we work hard to maintain a strong team culture across vast distances

  • Unlimited PTO — As well as 13 company holidays

  • Other Benefits — Employer-supported health, vision, and dental plans, subsidized parental leave, 3% 401(k) match, short- and long-term disability insurance, life and AD&D insurance, and a $1,000 annual professional development budget.

Role Specs

  • Reports to: Chief Growth Officer

  • Direct Reports: None currently; expected to build a small communications team over time as the function scales

  • Schedule: Full-time, flexible within U.S. time zones

  • Target start date: ASAP

  • Location: Remote, must be based in the U.S.

Highlights

CDI is seeking a VP of Strategic Comms to establish CDI as the leading national voice on constructive dialogue in higher education through earned media, executive visibility, and thought leadership.

title: Commercial Director - Flui
description:
Job Description:

About Us

Flui Technologies is a leading software solution provider to the energy and water sector, delivering innovative and scalable software infrastructure and services since 1990. Our solutions - MarketFlow, MeterFlow and DCC Adaptor - support market competition, smart metering, network flexibility and supplier integration across Energy Retail, Energy Networks and Water Retail, and are used to manage messaging for more than 35 million electricity and gas meter points.

As the utility sector evolves to meet the challenges of Net Zero, Smart Metering, Energy Code reform, Market-wide Half-Hourly Settlement, Demand-side Response and Embedded Generation, we combine deep industry knowledge with technical innovation to deliver robust, business-focused solutions backed by dedicated people and exceptional support.

The Role

The Commercial Director has overall ownership of the commercial engine of the business - sales, marketing and the bids/contracts function - across Flui's product and services portfolio. This is a director-level role with a seat on the leadership team, accountable for commercial strategy, revenue growth and profitable, sustainable client relationships across a regulated, technically complex market.

You will set the commercial direction for the business, own the commercial P&L, and provide strategic leadership, coaching and challenge to the sales and marketing team to deliver against ambitious company targets. The role combines strategic oversight - shaping go-to-market, pricing and partnership strategy - with close, hands-on involvement in our largest and most complex client relationships, tenders and framework agreements. You will work closely with the Managing Director, Chief Technology Officer, and Operations Director to ensure commercial strategy is joined up with product, delivery and customer success.

The post requires strong commercial judgement, multi-tasking, and the leadership and stakeholder-management skills to operate credibly from account teams through to utility C-suite and industry bodies.

Job Responsibilities

The Commercial Director will report to the Managing Director and will be responsible for:

  • Setting and owning the commercial strategy across sales, marketing and bids/contracts, aligned to Flui's growth targets in Energy Retail, Energy Networks and Water Retail.

  • Overseeing Account Management, New Business and Marketing activity to deliver annual bookings, revenue and retention targets, with full commercial P&L accountability.

  • Leading bid and tender strategy for formal procurement and framework processes typical of the utility sector, and personally sponsoring the largest, most strategic pursuits.

  • Developing pricing and packaging strategy across software licensing and managed services, balancing commercial growth with long-term client value.

  • Building and maintaining executive-level relationships with client organisations, industry bodies (e.g. Ofgem, Elexon, RECco etc) and partners across the energy and water sector.

  • Negotiating and structuring profitable, long-term commercial agreements and contracts with clients and partners.

  • Ensuring accurate sales reporting, pipeline management and forecasting, providing the Managing Director and leadership team with visibility of key commercial indicators.

  • Working closely with the CTO and product teams to ensure the commercial proposition reflects market needs - Net Zero, Smart Metering, Market-wide Half-Hourly Settlement and Energy Code reform - and feeds client insight back into the roadmap.

  • Recruiting, developing and motivating a high-performing sales and marketing team, and personally managing a small number of key accounts.

  • Ensuring an outstanding standard of commercial governance, contract compliance and customer service throughout the client lifecycle.

Essential Competencies and Experience

Business Acumen

  • Demonstrable understanding of the energy and/or water utility sector, including regulatory and market drivers such as Net Zero, Smart Metering and Market-wide Half-Hourly Settlement.

  • Track record of setting commercial strategy and driving profitable growth in a B2B software or technology business.

  • Experience with enterprise software solutions sold into large, complex and regulated organisations.

Commercial, Sales & Marketing Leadership

  • Significant experience in the UK energy, water or utilities sector, with knowledge of complex, long-cycle sales and formal tender/framework processes.

  • Experience building and leading successful sales and marketing teams, and managing a healthy, well-forecast pipeline.

  • Proven ability to build and maintain long-lasting relationships from operational contacts through to C-suite.

  • Excellent interpersonal and influencing skills across diverse professional backgrounds.

General

  • Strong experience of contract negotiation and commercial frameworks with both suppliers and customers.

  • Strong IT skills, including experience managing sales and pipeline through a CRM platform.

  • Willingness to travel across the UK, including occasional overnight stays.

Job Qualifications

  • A degree or equivalent in a relevant discipline is a bonus, or comparable director-level commercial experience.

  • An established profile and industry knowledge within the UK energy, water or utilities software sector is highly desirable.

Your Personal Characteristics Will Include

  • A great communicator with advanced negotiation and influencing skills at director/board level.

  • Commercially driven, with a hunter mindset balanced by strategic, long-term thinking.

  • An analytical mind, able to evaluate and evolve commercial approaches based on a strong understanding of business goals.

  • Results-driven and self-motivated, with a determination to close complex, high-value deals.

  • Highly organised, with a strong work ethic and the capacity to succeed in a demanding, regulated environment.

  • An understanding of the need to balance commercial success with customer satisfaction, regulatory compliance and employee engagement.

title: Full Stack Software Developer
description:
What You'll Do

  • Product & Application Development

  • Build and maintain modern web applications, from UI through to API and data layer.

  • Develop new product features and improve existing applications.

  • Integrate third-party APIs and external services.

  • Build internal tools and automations that remove manual work from business processes.

  • Translate business requirements into reliable, maintainable software.

  • Troubleshoot issues and improve application performance and reliability.

  • Participate in code reviews and help raise the bar on engineering practices.

Infrastructure & Operations

Infrastructure work is shared across a small team rather than siloed, so we're looking for someone who can contribute here credibly. How much of it lands with you will depend on your strengths and where the team needs help — but you should be comfortable with all of it.

  • Work with AWS infrastructure across production and non-production environments (EC2, ECS/EKS, Lambda, RDS, S3, VPC, IAM, CloudFront, Route 53).

  • Contribute to infrastructure defined as code using Terraform or CloudFormation.

  • Help maintain CI/CD pipelines and automated deployments, and improve the workflows around environments, releases, and debugging.

  • Contribute to monitoring, alerting, logging, and tracing — including dashboards and alerts that are actually actionable.

  • Take part in investigating production issues, root-cause analysis, and the follow-up fixes that prevent repeats.

  • Apply sound security practices: least-privilege IAM, network security, encryption, secrets management, and secure configuration.

  • Keep an eye on AWS spend — right-sizing, autoscaling, and retiring what isn't being used.

Required Qualifications

  • Several years building and shipping production web applications end to end.

  • Strong programming fundamentals in a modern typed or backend language, and the ability to become productive in a new one quickly.

  • Solid frontend skills: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and experience with a modern component framework (React or equivalent).

  • Hands-on experience running applications on AWS or a comparable cloud platform.

  • Practical experience with CI/CD pipelines, automated deployments, and infrastructure as code.

  • Comfort operating what you build — debugging production issues, reading logs and metrics, and improving reliability over time.

  • Experience with SQL and relational databases.

  • Experience integrating REST APIs and third-party services.

  • Git and pull-request-based collaboration.

  • Strong analytical skills and clear written and verbal communication.

Nice to Have

  • TypeScript.

  • Scala, Python, Go, or Node.js.

  • Terraform specifically, and container orchestration (ECS, EKS, or Kubernetes).

  • Observability tooling — metrics, logging, tracing, and alerting platforms.

  • Experience building applications on top of AI services or LLM APIs.

  • Familiarity with AI-assisted development tools such as GitHub Copilot, Cursor, or Claude Code.

  • Exposure to SOC 2 or similar compliance work.

  • Experience building automation or workflow tooling.

How You Work

  • You take initiative, take ownership, and follow work through to completion without needing to be chased.

  • You're resourceful and enjoy practical technical problems, including the unglamorous ones.

  • You pick up new technologies quickly and apply them sensibly.

  • You communicate clearly — progress, blockers, and technical decisions — and collaborate well.

  • You ship high-quality, practical solutions rather than over-engineering.

  • You have a product mindset and care whether the software actually creates impact.

What We Offer:

  • Direct impact: the products and systems you build are the ones the business runs on.

  • End-to-end ownership of meaningful projects, from idea through release and operation.

  • Unusual breadth for one role — product engineering and the infrastructure underneath it.

  • A collaborative environment focused on learning and continuous improvement.

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

About the Role

We're looking for a software developer who enjoys building things that solve real business problems — and who cares about how those things run once they're live.

This is a broad role in a small engineering organization. You'll build internal and customer-facing applications, prototype new ideas, and work close to the infrastructure those applications run on. If you like moving between product work and the systems side rather than staying in one lane, this role is designed for you.

Our stack is deliberately pragmatic rather than uniform: TypeScript and React on the frontend, with Scala, Python, Node.js, and Go across various services, all running on AWS. We care more about your engineering fundamentals than the specific languages on your resume — strong developers pick up a new stack quickly, and we'll give you the time to do it.

🌎 Fully remote — must be available to work US time zones (EST minimum)

title: Curative Landman - Oklahoma City, OK
description:
Purple Land Management is adding curative landmen to an active title curative project covering multiple drilling and spacing units in western Oklahoma(Roger Mills and Ellis Counties, OK). You’ll receive assigned requirements from division order title opinions and own them to closure. That means determining what each requirement is actually asking for, locating the people who have to act on it, contacting them directly, drafting the instrument, and getting it executed and recorded. Much of this work is independent and calls for sound judgment, because the owners you're contacting are usually not in this business and the records you're working from are often incomplete. You'll have a supervising landman to escalate to, and you're expected to recognize when a situation needs that.

Responsibilities

  • Review assigned requirements from division order title opinions, determine what each one requires, and identify the resolution path.
  • Locate the mineral owners, royalty owners, heirs, devisees, and successor entities named in each requirement using county records, probate and district court filings, obituaries, and public search resources.
  • Contact owners by telephone, mail, and email, explain the requirement and the instrument you're asking them to sign in plain language without giving legal advice, and manage the execution logistics including notary coordination and return mailings.
  • Draft the curative instruments, including stipulations of interest, stipulations of interest and cross-conveyance, disclaimers, affidavits of heirship, corrective assignments, quitclaim deeds, and ratifications, with accurate legal descriptions, decimal interests, exhibits, and signature blocks matched to the capacity in which each party signs.
  • File and record executed instruments with the county clerk and track each one through recording.
  • Maintain organized records of every contact, response, and mailing in the curative contact log, and communicate status, obstacles, and items that need escalation to the supervising landman.

Required Qualifications

  • Prior experience handling title curative work.
  • Ability to read a division order title opinion, understand what each requirement is asking for, and recognize where the defect sits in the chain of title.
  • Working knowledge of common title defects and how they're cured in practice, including probates, affidavits, powers of attorney, and corrective instruments.
  • Comfort communicating with mineral and royalty owners outside the industry by telephone and in writing. Many of the owners you'll contact are elderly, recently bereaved, cautious about unsolicited calls, or unaware they own an interest at all.
  • Careful drafting from confirmed facts only. Every recital in a curative instrument has to trace to a recorded document, the title opinion, or information the owner has verified, and the discipline to stop and ask rather than fill a gap with an assumption is part of the job.
  • Independent judgment, the ability to prioritize and track a list of open requirements sitting at different stages, and proficiency in Google Workspace.
Company Description
Purple Land Management, LLC (“Purple”) is one of the nation’s largest tech-enabled providers of land services that negotiates the buying, selling, and leasing of energy rights, determines and cures title, prepares mineral ownership reports, and performs other related services required for all types of energy companies. Overdrive, Purple’s proprietary software-as-a-service (“SaaS”), allows customers to track lease, well, and contract data in a web-based geographic information system (“GIS”) mapping platform powered by ESRI, a leader in GIS mapping software. Based in Fort Worth, Texas, and founded in 2010, Purple has the financial support of Satori Capital, a Texas-based multi-strategy investment firm founded upon the principles of conscious capitalism. Satori’s private equity business partners with leadership teams of companies that operate with a long-term perspective, commit to their mission, and create value for all stakeholders.
